studies with one or more official **paid** work terms within their area of
study. The difference between a co-op work term and an internship is duration and

## CO-OP overview

MSFEA CO-OP combines study with a full-time and paid work term of at least 6 months, associated with FEAA 500. It is an optional program. Apply to the program at least one year before your intended start. Eligibility requirements include a minimum GPA of 3.3 at application and course enrollment, at least 90 completed credits when enrolling in FEAA 500 (120 for architecture), and completion of the required career development modules before applying to positions and enrolling; departments may impose additional requirements. Students who pass FEAA 500 are no longer required to take their department's Approved Experience / Professional Training course. The application stages, conditions, tuition, work responsibilities and deliverables are explained below.

## Motivation and benefits

- **For students:** a co-op lets students immerse themselves in an industry and
  better understand their field. A paid, extended placement builds a stronger
  sense of responsibility and makes the experience more meaningful. Research shows
  co-op participation increases student interest in learning and academic
  performance on return to campus, and leads to more satisfying career outcomes
  (Blair et al., 2004; Boudreau and Marx, 2019).

## Approved Experience internship and CO-OP comparison

The department's Approved Experience internship is a graduation requirement. It
requires at least **8 weeks** of approved training and can be unpaid (see the
Summer Training Guidelines). MSFEA
CO-OP is an optional, full-time paid work term of at least **6 months**. Students
who pass FEAA 500 are no longer required to take their department's Approved
Experience / Professional Training course. The CO-OP rules and substitution are
specified in this handbook; the internship minimum comes from the Summer Training
Guidelines.

Topic: MSFEA CO-OP (Cooperative Education) Handbook > Information for students > The FEAA 500 course
### The FEAA 500 course

A student who accepts an offer enrolls in **FEAA 500 in both semesters** of the
co-op position (Summer and Fall, or Spring and Summer):

- **First semester:** register **FEAA 500** (3 credits) and pay its tuition.
- **Second semester:** register **FEAA 500A** (3 credits) with **no additional tuition** (no additional tuition fees).

Full-time student status is maintained in both semesters. A student with
satisfactory performance at the end of the first co-op semester receives a grade
of **"In Progress (PR)"** on FEAA 500; the final **Pass or Fail** grade is
assigned on **FEAA 500A** at the end of the second semester.

**Question/topic:** Are six company internship weeks alone enough for EECE 500?

For ECE, one documented way to complete a six-week company placement is two weeks of research with an MSFEA faculty member; the company and research components must be approved and documented. As an exchange program, MSFEA CDC also hosts incoming international students for internships in Lebanon.
